lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: I'd like to call this meeting to order. Well, council, it's my turn to do opening, and next week we have the Manitoba Chamber of Commerce is coming to do their AGM in our event centre. First time they've ever done this event in our city, and so there'll be chambers of commerce from just about every city or municipality in Manitoba, so it'll be a great time to showcase our community. So I've been working on— I have— there's a couple of times where I have to speak and make— bring greetings and messages from the city. So I've been working on some stuff, and I've been finding some really neat, interesting facts about Steinbach. So I'm going to— you'll be my guinea pigs. I'll use you as part of it. Yeah. It's going to be changing. I'll be polishing this, but this is something along the lines of one of my speeches will be. The city of Steinbach has a surprisingly strong and well-rounded economic base. Okay, thank you. For a mid-sized Canadian city, its strengths are not abstract, but as a matter of fact, they are quite concrete and measurable across several areas. Number one, Steinbach has a very diverse— diversified economic structure. Steinbach's biggest advantage is that it does not rely on just one single industry. Our core sectors include manufacturing, healthcare, a large retail component, which is made up of large— which makes up a large portion of the jobs in our city. We also have additional businesses in transportation, construction, finance, and technology. Diversity like this provides resilience because when one sector slows, the others can compensate. Steinbach is a major hub for a large— the large surrounding region. Steinbach serves as a main shopping services and agricultural supply hub for a wide rural area. Its training area exceeds 150,000 people, far larger than the city itself. Thank you. And it— this gives it its outsized economic influence relative to its population. Unlike many small cities, Steinbach has a significant industrial capacity. Large employers like Loewen Windows provide stable, higher-paying jobs with export-oriented economic activity with money coming from outside the region. Steinbach has a powerful agro- Agribusiness ecosystem. Steinbach isn't just agriculture. It integrates farming with processing, logistics, and innovation. This integration is a high-value economic model, not just raw commodity production. Rapid population and workforce growth. Steinbach is one of the fastest-growing cities in Manitoba. Population increased 32% from 2011 to 2021, and our workforce grew at that same time by 30%. Growth is good. It expands our labor pool, attracts investments and local demand for housing and retail and services. Another fact that I found out during this time, in 2025, our population was 20,011 people, and we're Projected to reach by 2045, 36,936 people. That's a significant amount. That actually doubles the amount from the amount of increase from 2020, 2011, or 20— yeah, 2020-11 to 2021. And some more facts. In 2010, I was voted on council. Councillor Susan Penner, we got on at the same time. Since that time, there were 2,268 dwelling units added to our city. You know, the thought of door knocking this fall scares me. 'Cause it's like 50% more. Since 2010, there was also $909,645,189 of total, the total value of building permits in that time. And then from 2016 to 2025, there was a total value of $137,989,189. Order. $139 of infrastructure that's been added to our city. Some of that's donated through development, but much of that's done through the city's— our council infrastructure renewal program. Another one of our strengths is our ability to attract workers. About 28% of our workforce is immigrant-based. Strong immigration helps solve a common rural problem throughout our area, and that is labor shortage. Steinbach has marketed itself on affordability. We have one of the lowest municipal tax rates in Manitoba. Lower cost attracts business and residents. Lower cost creates a pro-growth environment, and Steinbach City Council has always been pro-growth and business-friendly. Our location is an important advantage as well. We are less than 1 hour away from Winnipeg, which is a major logistics hub, and we're close to the U.S. border. We have 2 major highways that intersect in our city. This supports trade and exports, supply chain efficiencies, and access to large markets without big city costs. Steinbach has disproportionately large retail sector for its size. Retail is one of its largest employment sectors of our city, and this reflects Steinbach's role as a regional consumer hub. Steinbach's total income generated annually is about $844 million. For a city that has a population around 20,000, that is a very strong per capita economic footprint. All put together, Steinbach is not just another small prairie city. It's a regional economic engine with unusual strong fundamentals for its size. Thank you. Council, we have the agenda in front of us, looking for a motion to adopt. Councillor Penner. Seconded by Councillor Hiebert. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. Council, we have the minutes. Uh, in front of us from April 7th, 2026, regular council meeting. Looking for a motion to approve. Second. Second by Councillor Zwaagstra. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. Uh, council, is any business arising from the minutes? Okay, seeing none, uh, council, at this time I would like a— to have a motion to excuse Councillor Jac Siemens. Councillor Penner. Second by Councillor Hiebert. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. We are just a little after 7:35, so we'll go directly into the public hearing. Council, we have 6A, variance V2026-07. This is referring to 225 Croeker Avenue. At this time, I will call We'll close the council meeting, open the public hearing. Mr. Warkentin, can you please introduce this file?

lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. There is a report on page 80 of council's agenda package. I'll refer to it, at least a few lines in it, as my introduction. The city has several major drains and waterways running through it. The drainage patterns in Steinbach generally move from a southeast to a northwest direction. One of these drains, the Manning Canal, is a designated provincial waterway and enters city limits at its southeastern boundary at the intersection of Hanover Road East and Hirschfeld Road. The canal provides surface water drainage capacity for the city's east and north quadrants and exits the city along Keating Road just to the south. Okay. And south of Clear Springs Road West. There has been extensive negotiations ongoing between the city and Manitoba Transportation and Infrastructure over the better part of 2 years, with the first ideas first being discussed in 2022, in which the City of Steinbach had requested consideration from the province Yes. To be transferred full jurisdiction and authority over this particular drain, as it is the only drain running through the City of Steinbach that is still under full provincial jurisdiction. There was some support from the provincial department in order to do that, and because legislation requires that a formal transfer of jurisdiction from Manitoba to The change to the city would require a lieutenant governor and council decision. For practical purposes, the negotiation and authorization to enter into this memorandum of understanding agreement was seen as an appropriate first step, as the change in legislation can take significantly longer than the negotiation of this agreement has already taken. Long story short, recommendation from administration is that city council approve the city entering into this agreement so that the official transfer of jurisdiction can proceed in due course.

lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. This is an application to amend City of Steinbach zoning bylaw 2245, and this zoning bylaw amendment is bylaw 2275. The application seeks the city's approval to add a definition of transitional housing Okay. I'd like to move that amendment to the City of Steinbach zoning bylaw where transitional housing means temporary supportive housing intended to bridge the gap from being either unhoused or in unstable living conditions into a more permanent housing setting. Occupancy is typically short to medium term, generally ranging from 3 months to 3 years, and may include supportive services such as case management, counseling, and life skills training to assist residents in achieving independence. Okay. The application also requests that this particular definition within the zoning bylaw be considered as a permitted use in the C-2 commercial community zone. And with respect to the application, This is being applied for by— sorry, [name withheld] and representatives of Vee Inn. With respect to first reading of city council, administration has reviewed the application. Thank you. And the city planner has also provided a report for council's consideration related to background of this bylaw. And upon review of the application and the nature of it being to amend the general policies of the city zoning bylaw, administration is of the opinion that the proposed definition should be more broadly worded while still retaining the intent of the application. An amended definition is provided in the package, which also attempts to avoid perceived stigmas related to how potential residents may come to use or be a resident at such a site. Secondly, the application also seeks to add transitional housing as a permitted use in the C-2 commercial community zone, and hereto, the proposal seeks to amend the general policy Thank you. the city's zoning bylaw and administration is of the opinion that transitional housing may be added as a use in Table 10-1, but as a conditional use, and that the number of zones be expanded to include those as noted in the city planner's report. If this use is added as a conditional use, it would be better aligned with the existing land use policies that the city already has in place. Most residential or residential-related uses in the commercial zones under use table 10-1 are either conditional or not permitted under the city zoning bylaw 2245. Finally, administration also recommends that the term transitional housing be added as a use type on table 7-3 pertaining to required onsite parking spaces, where those would be recommended to be one space every 5 dwelling units or beds. Again, this is being recommended because these requirements would be similar to a group or to a category that currently contains group homes, group residences, neighborhood rehabilitation homes, and assisted living facilities. Other options that council may wish to consider would be to also approve first reading to Bylaw 2275 as applied for. With further amendments to be considered at second reading. Council could also deny first reading. However, given the nature of the application, administration recommends council approve first reading subject to the amendments as I've noted to the definition, the use table, and the parking table. And if first reading is approved, a public hearing could be scheduled for a future council meeting. Thank you.

lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. I will support the motion. And so the key thing here is that it would be a conditional use, which is what an emergency residential shelter would be. It's also, frankly, what an apartment building would be if it was in a commercial zone. That's also an example of a conditional use. There are many different categories of projects that fall under conditional use in these types of areas, and the reason for that is very simple. Thank you. This is the type of facility that could change the character of a neighbourhood, and when you have something that could change the character of a neighbourhood, it makes sense to have a public hearing because at that public hearing, the applicant comes forward with a full and finalized plan and presents it in a public setting, and then also the neighbourhood has a chance to come and hear the presentation and then have any questions— raise any questions and raise any concerns, and then the applicant has an opportunity to respond. That is the benefit of a public hearing. I mean, we just did public hearings for some variances as small as like a couple of feet in terms of side yards and such. And we can— that is obviously important enough that we would have a public hearing for those kinds of variances. For a project of this significance, it's fully reasonable that it would be a conditional use so that way a public hearing would be triggered. So I would not support it being a permitted use because that would mean that it would be a blanket across these zoning categories across the city, there would be no public hearing required in terms of where this— if this facility is proposed to be built in a certain location or any location for that matter. So I think the motion is a sensible one. This would lead to a public hearing in regards to this change in the zoning category. And then if this change goes in, then it goes into the bylaw. And then if an organization wishes to apply for transitional housing, There would be a public hearing for a specific site-specific property. And that's why the conditional use is so important, because it ensures that it— there will be a site-specific public hearing whenever an application is made for this type of housing, as there should be.

lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Bill Hiebert (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. It's good to see, uh, new businesses coming to Steinbach to apply for licenses. There's 9 new applications, and I see no reason but to approve.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further?

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. Councillor Hiebert has made a compelling case. I, I'm happy to second his motion.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, anything further, council, in closing?

lines.speaker: Bill Hiebert
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Bill Hiebert (Councillor) [medium]
lines.text: Nothing.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Call for the question. All in favor? Opposed? That was carried. Council, we've come to council question period. Are there any questions of council? Okay, seeing none, we'll end off correspondence petitions. We've got 11A. This is Minister of Municipality and Northern Relations. This is our 2025 Mobility Disadvantaged Transportation Program. It's our final payment for the year. Looks like we're getting $15,000 grant for Mobility disadvantaged transportation program. Mr. Thiessen, this just gets forwarded to the Pat Porter Active Living Centre for—

lines.speaker: Adam Thiessen
lines.title: Senior Manager, Corporate Services
lines.label: Adam Thiessen (Senior Manager, Corporate Services)
lines.text: Yes, that's correct.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: For running the service for us.

lines.speaker: Adam Thiessen
lines.title: Senior Manager, Corporate Services
lines.label: Adam Thiessen (Senior Manager, Corporate Services)
lines.text: Yep, that's correct. Yeah, they pay us in 2 installments every year for a total of $30,000.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, council, how would you like to take this information? And we've got the FCM Green Municipal Fund enhancing the recreation experience at Steinbach Soccer Park through tree planting. So they are, we've been approved for a grant for the amount of $67,160. I guess that will plant a fair number of trees in the soccer park. Looks good. Um, so, um, council, how would you like to proceed to take this information at this time? Okay, there's no other business. Looking for a motion to adjourn.

lines.speaker: Bill Hiebert
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Bill Hiebert (Councillor) [medium]
lines.text: Second.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Second by Councillor Hiebert. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That's carried. Next regular council meeting is Tuesday, May 5th, 2026, 7:30 PM.
